death.crash: The geometry engine crashed{detail}. Save your work, then restart SindriCAD.
death.portInUse: SindriCAD could not start its geometry engine: {cause}. Another copy of SindriCAD may still be running. Close it and open SindriCAD again.
death.portInUseDefault: its port is already in use
death.startupFailure: The geometry engine could not start{detail}. Modelling is unavailable until you restart SindriCAD. If it happens again, {reportHere}.

engine.down: the geometry engine is not running; restart SindriCAD

error.badRequest: the geometry engine rejected this request (update SindriCAD)
error.bodyTooLarge: this body is too large to process
error.budgetExhausted: this operation ran out of its time budget
error.cutLostProjection: Cut removed nothing: its profile is placed by a projected edge in {sketch} that lost the edge it was projected from (drawn amber), so the profile may not be where you meant it. Edit {sketch}, delete the amber edge, pick the edge again with Project, then move the profile back where you want it and dimension it to the new edge. If the profile is already where you meant it, drag the other way, or use Join.

cutOnlyHidden.one: This cut removed nothing: the only body it reaches is {body}, which was hidden when you made the cut, so I left it alone. To cut it, delete this cut, show {body} and make the cut again.
cutOnlyHidden.other: This cut removed nothing: the only bodies it reaches, {body} and others ({count} in all), were hidden when you made the cut, so I left them alone. To cut them, delete this cut, show them and make the cut again.

error.engineUnavailable: the geometry engine is not running; restart SindriCAD
error.insertNoBodies: That document has no visible bodies to insert. Bodies hidden there are left out.
error.insertNothingBuilt: Nothing in that document built, so there is nothing to insert. Open it to see what failed.

joinPiecesApart.one: {count} piece I joined into {body} does not touch the rest of it, so after this step it is a separate piece of the body. A gap too small to see still counts. Make it overlap to fuse it in, or use Separate into bodies to give it a body of its own.
joinPiecesApart.other: {count} pieces I joined into {body} do not touch the rest of it, so after this step they are separate pieces of the body. A gap too small to see still counts. Make them overlap to fuse them in, or use Separate into bodies to give each a body of its own.

joinPiecesLeftOut.one: I left {count} piece out of the join because it is under a thousandth of the joined body's size and does not touch it. Any gap counts, however small: make it overlap the body to keep it.
joinPiecesLeftOut.other: I left {count} pieces out of the join because each is under a thousandth of the joined body's size and does not touch it. Any gap counts, however small: make them overlap the body to keep them.

error.kernelCrashed: the geometry kernel crashed on this operation

mergeAllDamaged.one: Merge changed nothing: the only solid part of {body} is damaged, and I leave damaged parts out rather than repair them.
mergeAllDamaged.other: Merge changed nothing: all {count} solid parts of {body} are damaged, and I leave damaged parts out rather than repair them.

mergeDamagedLeftOut.one: {count} solid part of {body} is damaged, so I left it out of the merge rather than repair it. Whatever it covered is missing from the result.
mergeDamagedLeftOut.other: {count} solid parts of {body} are damaged, so I left them out of the merge rather than repair them. Whatever they covered is missing from the result.

mergeDroppedSurfaces.one: I dropped {count} loose surface from {body}. It had no thickness, so it cannot be printed; if part of the shape existed only as that surface, it is now open or missing.
mergeDroppedSurfaces.other: I dropped {count} loose surfaces from {body}. They had no thickness, so they cannot be printed; if part of the shape existed only as those surfaces, it is now open or missing.

error.mergeFailed: Merge failed on {body}: the geometry kernel could not fuse its solids into a sound one that holds all of them. Nothing was changed.
error.mergeNoBody: Merge: the body it was made on does not exist at this point in the timeline.
error.mergeNoSolid: Merge changed nothing: {body} has no solid parts, only surfaces, so there is nothing to merge. Thicken turns a surface into a solid.
error.mergeNothing: {body} is already one solid, so there is nothing to merge.

mergeNothingApart.other: {body} is already {count} separate solids that do not touch, so there is nothing to merge. Separate into bodies makes each of them a body of its own.

mergeSeparatePieces.other: {body} is now {count} separate pieces that do not touch. Separate into bodies splits them apart.

error.replyTooLarge: the result is too large to display
error.rustImportUnsupported: geometry import isn't supported by the Rust backend yet — run without VITE_GEOM=rust
error.rustInterferenceUnsupported: interference check isn't supported by the Rust backend yet — run without VITE_GEOM=rust

separateDroppedFaces.one: I left out {count} loose face of {body}: Separate makes a body from each of its surfaces, and this face is not joined into any of them, so it did not become a body. If part of the shape existed only as that face, it is now open or missing.
separateDroppedFaces.other: I left out {count} loose faces of {body}: Separate makes a body from each of its surfaces, and these faces are not joined into any of them, so they did not become bodies. If part of the shape existed only as those faces, it is now open or missing.

separateDroppedSurfaces.one: I left out {count} loose surface of {body}: it has no thickness, so it did not become a body. If part of the shape existed only as that surface, it is now open or missing.
separateDroppedSurfaces.other: I left out {count} loose surfaces of {body}: they have no thickness, so they did not become bodies. If part of the shape existed only as those surfaces, it is now open or missing.

splitBodiesGone.one: {count} of the bodies this split was made on does not exist at this point in the timeline, so I cut only the others.
splitBodiesGone.other: {count} of the bodies this split was made on do not exist at this point in the timeline, so I cut only the others.

error.splitCrashed: Split crashed the geometry kernel, so nothing was split. Moving the plane slightly with an offset may help.
error.splitDamaged: Split changed nothing: every part of {body} that the plane crosses is damaged, and I leave damaged parts whole rather than cut them.

splitDamagedAll.one: Split changed nothing: the one part of {body} that the plane crosses is damaged, and the plane does not pass through the other selected bodies. I leave damaged parts whole rather than cut them.
splitDamagedAll.other: Split changed nothing: the {count} parts of {body} that the plane crosses are damaged, and the plane does not pass through the other selected bodies. I leave damaged parts whole rather than cut them.

splitDamagedAllMore.one: Split changed nothing: {count} of the selected bodies, {body}, has damaged parts crossing the plane ({parts} in all), and the plane cuts nothing else. I leave damaged parts whole rather than cut them.
splitDamagedAllMore.other: Split changed nothing: {count} of the selected bodies, {body} among them, have damaged parts crossing the plane ({parts} in all), and the plane cuts nothing else. I leave damaged parts whole rather than cut them.

splitDamagedParts.one: {count} part of {body} crosses the plane but is damaged, so I left it whole.
splitDamagedParts.other: {count} parts of {body} cross the plane but are damaged, so I left them whole.

error.splitFaceGone: Split: the face the splitting plane was taken from is gone, because its body does not exist at this point in the timeline. Pick the splitting plane again.
error.splitFailed: Split failed on {body}: the geometry kernel could not cut it. Nothing was changed.
error.splitLegacyFailed: Split failed on {body}: this split was made in an older version, which could not cut it. Edit the split and press OK to cut it part by part.
error.splitLegacyVolume: The pieces of {body} do not add up to the body this split cut: some of its parts are damaged, and this split was made in an older version, which cut damaged parts anyway. Edit the split and press OK to cut it part by part, which leaves damaged parts whole.
error.splitMissed: Split changed nothing: the plane does not pass through {body}.
error.splitMissedAll: Split changed nothing: the plane does not pass through any of the selected bodies.
error.splitNoBody: Split: nothing it was made to cut exists at this point in the timeline. Edit the split and pick the bodies to cut again.
error.splitNoPlane: Split: the plane this cut uses does not exist at this point in the timeline. Pick the splitting plane again.
error.splitOnFace: Split changed nothing: the plane lies on a face of {body} and does not pass through it. Give the cut an offset to move it into the body.
error.splitSeparated: Nothing solid was cut through on {body}: the plane only separated the parts on each side of it.
error.splitSeparatedKept: Nothing solid was cut through on {body}: I kept the parts on the side you chose and removed the ones on the other side.
error.stoppedByOther: stopped because another operation was cancelled, try again
error.timedOut: operation timed out — geometry too complex or degenerate
error.tooLarge: This model is too large for the geometry engine: {size} MiB, and the limit is {limit} MiB. Remove or simplify the imported body, then try again.
error.tooLargeRefused: That model is too large for the geometry engine to accept. Remove or simplify the imported body, then try again.
error.unknownOp: the geometry engine does not know this operation (update SindriCAD)

engine.reportHere: click the bug button in the bottom-right corner so I get the log

warning.splitMissed: The plane does not pass through {body}, so I left it as it was.

wire.incomplete: the geometry engine's reply was incomplete
wire.manifestMismatch: the geometry engine sent a body that did not match its manifest
wire.outOfOrder: the geometry engine's reply arrived out of order
wire.restarted: the geometry engine restarted its reply mid-send
wire.stalledMidReply: the geometry engine stopped part-way through its reply
wire.unreadable: the geometry engine sent an unreadable reply

ref.edgeNotStraight: That edge isn't straight. Pick a straight edge, a corner or a face.
ref.faceCurved: That face is curved. An extrude can only start from a flat face parallel to its sketch.
ref.faceTilted: That face is tilted to the sketch. For now an extrude can only start from a face parallel to its sketch. Pick a parallel face, or a corner of this one.
ref.lineNotParallel: That line isn't parallel to the sketch, so it doesn't say where to start or stop. Pick a line parallel to the sketch, a point, or a face.
ref.noBody: I can't tell which body that belongs to. Pick it again, or pick a face or a plane.
ref.noProfile: Pick the profile to extrude first.
ref.noReply: I couldn't read that pick. Is the geometry engine running? Try the click again.
ref.notStraight: That sketch curve isn't a straight line. Pick a straight line or a point.
ref.planeTilted: That plane is tilted to the sketch. For now an extrude can only start from a plane parallel to its sketch.
ref.unsupported: This geometry engine can't store a pick on a body. Pick a sketch point, a sketch line or a plane instead.

gpu.spoofedNote: The renderer name above comes from the Linux webview, which reports the same fake value on every machine. Ignore it. The WebGL version line is real.
gpu.title: The 3D view could not start
gpu.tryThese: Two things are worth trying. Close SindriCAD, then start it again from a terminal with one of these in front of the usual command:

why.noWebgl: This computer could not create a 3D context of any kind. That usually means the graphics driver is missing or is being blocked, rather than anything wrong with SindriCAD itself.
why.renderer: This computer reports WebGL 2, but the 3D view still could not be created. That is unusual, and I would like to see the report.
why.webgl1Only: This computer's graphics driver offers OpenGL ES 2.0 only, and the 3D view needs WebGL 2. That is a limit of the driver, not a damaged install. On Linux it usually means an older NVIDIA card running on the open-source nouveau driver.

gpu.workaroundNote: The first draws in software on the CPU. It is slower on large models, but it works where the driver does not. The second turns off the webview's shared-buffer path, which some drivers do not implement correctly.

check.title: Sketch check

constraint.alreadyPicked: That is the point you already picked — choose the second one to mirror.
constraint.boundShape: I did not apply that: it needs the {shape}'s {field} to change, and a parameter sets it. Change the parameter instead.
constraint.coincidentMiss: Nothing to put together there. Coincident takes a point (an end, a corner, a centre or a sketch point), then a second point to join it to, or the line, circle or arc to put it on. Click two lines to make them Collinear.
constraint.collinearApplied: Two lines: applied Collinear. To put a point on a line, click the point and the line.
constraint.conflict: That constraint conflicts with the ones already on this sketch, so it was not applied.
constraint.equalMismatch: Equal needs two lines, or two circles/arcs — a length and a radius are not comparable.
constraint.filletRadiusConflict: The fillet was created, but its radius could not be constrained without conflicting with this sketch's existing constraints.
constraint.glyphDelete: Click to delete this constraint (double- or right-click if it sits on geometry)
constraint.glyphPending: Will be applied when you click
constraint.pointOnNeedsPoint: Coincident puts a point on a curve, so one of the two clicks has to be a point: an end, a corner, a centre or a sketch point.
constraint.pointOnOwnCurve: That point belongs to the curve you picked. Put it on a different line, circle or arc.
constraint.samePointTwice: That is the same point twice — Coincident joins two DIFFERENT points.
constraint.sameShape: Those are two points of the same shape — joining them would collapse it.
constraint.tangentSpan: I could not keep that circle touching the edge it is tangent to, so this constraint was not applied. The only solutions I found move the touch point off that edge.

error.centreOnLine: That circle's centre lies on the line — there is no edge-to-edge distance to dimension.
error.coincidentPoints: Those two points are coincident — the distance measures 0, nothing to drive.
error.collinearLines: Those lines are collinear — the distance measures 0, nothing to drive.
error.concentric: These circles are concentric — centre distance is 0. Dimension each diameter, or right-click → Pick Circle/Arc Tangent before each pick for the radial gap (wall thickness).
error.lineCrosses: That line crosses the circle — there is no edge-to-edge distance to dimension. Dimension the centre to the line instead.
error.lineTangent: That line is tangent to the circle — the edge-to-edge distance measures 0, nothing to drive.
error.mustBeNonZero: must evaluate to a non-zero value
error.mustBePositive: must evaluate to a positive value
error.noExpression: this dimension can't hold an expression yet
error.overlapping: These two circles overlap — there is no edge-to-edge clearance to dimension. Dimension their centres, or each diameter.
error.ownCentreAndRim: That is the circle's own centre and rim — dimension its radius instead.
error.pointAtCentre: That point sits at the circle's centre — the distance to its edge IS its radius, so dimension the radius instead.
error.pointOnCircle: That point lies on the circle — the distance to the edge measures 0, nothing to drive.
error.pointOnLine: That point lies on the line — the distance measures 0, nothing to drive.
error.rimsTouch: These two rims touch — the edge-to-edge distance measures 0, nothing to drive.
error.sameCircleTwice: That is one circle picked twice — pick a second entity to measure to.
error.sameRim: These two rims are the same circle — the radial gap measures 0.
error.slotWidth: That is the slot's width, which the slot sets itself. To change it, edit the slot's width dimension.
error.unsupported: A {kind} can't be dimensioned there. Pick a line, an arc, a circle, or a side or corner of a rectangle, polygon or slot.

dimension.fixedEndsNotApplied: Both ends are fixed reference geometry, so this dimension can only measure — the value you typed was not applied.

prompt.rotate: Rotate: click the center to turn about (it snaps to points), then type an angle + Enter · Esc
prompt.rotateChoose: Rotate: click what to rotate · Shift or Ctrl-click adds more · Enter to continue · Esc
prompt.scale: Scale: click the base point to scale from (it snaps to points), then type a factor + Enter · Esc
prompt.scaleChoose: Scale: click what to scale · Shift or Ctrl-click adds more · Enter to continue · Esc
prompt.select: Select: click a curve, an end, a corner, a centre or one side of a shape to pick it · double-click for the whole shape or chain · Shift- or Ctrl-click (Cmd on a Mac) adds or removes · drag a box to select several · right-click to constrain what is picked · drag to move · Delete to remove · while drawing, hold Ctrl to place without snapping · or pick a tool: Line (L) · Rectangle (R) · Circle (C) · Arc (A)
prompt.slot: Slot: click the two arc centers, then a point for the width · Esc
prompt.spline: Spline: click to place fit points · click the last point or press Enter to finish · Esc to cancel
prompt.symmetric: Symmetric: click two endpoints, then the symmetry axis line · Esc
prompt.tangent: Tangent: click two curves (line, circle or arc) to make them tangent · Esc
prompt.trim: Trim: click a curve (line/arc/circle) to remove it up to the nearest crossings · Esc
prompt.vertical: Vertical: click a line to make it vertical · Esc

solver.cspBlocked: The 2D constraint solver could not start: this build's security policy blocks the code it needs to initialise. That is a bug in SindriCAD, not a problem with your system, so updating your webview or graphics drivers will not help. Sketching still works, but without constraints, dimensions or point dragging.
solver.failed: The 2D constraint solver could not start: {detail}
solver.stopped: The 2D constraint solver stopped responding — sketching continues without constraints

text.notDrawn: I could not draw this text: {reason}. Edit it or pick another font to try again.
text.notDrawnRetry: I could not draw this text: {reason}. I will try again when the geometry engine is back.

transform.areaNotCurves: I move, copy, turn and scale lines and curves, not the area inside a shape. Click the shape's lines and curves (Shift or Ctrl-click adds more), then press Enter.
transform.choseOnlyThis: I selected just that one, as a plain click does, and let the others go. Shift or Ctrl-click adds instead. Press Enter once everything is selected.
transform.moveTied: I did not move anything: a constraint ties what you selected to geometry that is not being moved, and the solver would pull it back or stretch it. Select that geometry too, or remove the constraint, then move again.
transform.pressEnter: Press Enter once everything is selected, then click the point to work from.

rectangleToLines.one: A rectangle always sits square to the sketch axes, so I turned it into four lines kept square to each other and rotated those. Its constraints moved to the lines.
rectangleToLines.other: A rectangle always sits square to the sketch axes, so I turned these {count} into lines kept square to each other and rotated those. Their constraints moved to the lines.

transform.rotatePrompt: Rotate: type an angle in degrees
transform.rotateTied: I did not rotate anything: a constraint ties what you selected to geometry that is not being rotated, and the solver would pull it back part of the way. Select that geometry too, or remove the constraint, then rotate again.
transform.selectFirstCopy: Nothing is selected yet. Click what to copy (Shift or Ctrl-click adds more), then press Enter.
transform.selectFirstMove: Nothing is selected yet. Click what to move (Shift or Ctrl-click adds more), then press Enter.
transform.selectFirstRotate: Nothing is selected yet. Click what to rotate (Shift or Ctrl-click adds more), then press Enter.
transform.selectFirstScale: Nothing is selected yet. Click what to scale (Shift or Ctrl-click adds more), then press Enter.
